Other convulsive disorders Disorders that feature convulsions or epileptic seizures but are not considered to be forms of epilepsy are described below. Alcohol withdrawal syndrome. For a discussion of the management of seizures associated with alcohol with- drawal syndrome, see p.1626. Eclampsia and pre-eclampsia. Pre-eclampsia is a hy- pertensive disorder occurring in pregnancy that entails in- creased blood pressure together with proteinuria, and sometimes abnormal coagulation, liver dysfunction, and oedema; rarely the disorder may progress to eclampsia, which is a convulsive phase.
